title: Back from the hospital: Larkin's uniform and his mother's objection
summary: After the hospital Cobb rehearses with Milton Larkin, who brings his uniform; his mother protests but her sister persuades her to let him go.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, look, where did we leave off with your career -- oh, you've come back with plurisy.

All right, I came back -- I was sick. I went in the hospital; I had plurisy, and Milt Larkin, after I come out of the hospital -- I was at Jefferson Davis, and I was doing mighty fine; I was waiting on people in the hospital, and walking around because I was young -- too young to die.

I come home and I get my horn out from under the bed, and go to rehearsal and my mother came over on, like, a Thursday night -- and this is unusual, and she knew I'd been through hell and high water with the illness, and I've living with my aunt at this time; her favorite sister, and Milton Larkin brought my uniform over, and let me tell you, that uniform was a white jacket and tuxedo trousers; and oh, it was sharp. I was the sharpest -- that was our uniform.
And we'd get ready on Friday night; this is Thursday, to play the Preview Alumni dance.
Preview A & M College right up there; it's a state institution, college. And we were playing at the Harlem Grill on Friday night, which is the next night. My
mother performed! And she told him to 'Get that damn uniform out of here because he ain't gonna wear it.' Yes, she did. She didn't know I had rehearsed already, and pulled the horn out.

My aunt talked to her and said, 'You turn that boy loose and let him do what he wants to do. You've got him on your apron strings and you're gonna kill him.' And that's her favorite sister, and you don't know how much I admired her for saying that, and they cried and they carried on ... but she turned me loose, and I've been going ever since.
Well, I mean, she was concerned about you coming home from Dallas.
Well, see, it made good sense ...
But that's all she ... I'm the only child, and the doctor already said I had just so much time to live.
